claim: Inactivating mutations in the melanocortin 4 receptor (MC4R) gene cause monogenic obesity.
source: Inactivating mutations in the melanocortin 4 receptor (MC4R) gene cause monogenic obesity.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field, supported by citations in the manuscript (Farooqi et al., 2003; Balthasar et al., 2005).

claim: Female patients with MC4R mutations display various degrees of reproductive disorders.
source: Interestingly, female patients also display various degrees of reproductive disorders, in line with the subfertile phenotype of Mc4r KO female mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to human studies (Hainerová et al., 2011; Doulla et al., 2014; Batarfi et al., 2019) mentioned later in the manuscript.

claim: Mc4r KO female mice display a subfertile phenotype.
source: Interestingly, female patients also display various degrees of reproductive disorders, in line with the subfertile phenotype of Mc4r KO female mice.
evidence: This is supported by citations to mouse studies (Chen et al., 2017; Sandrock et al., 2009; Cui et al., 2022) mentioned in the manuscript.

claim: Mc4r expressed in Kiss1 neurons regulates fertility in females.
source: Here, we show that Mc4r expressed in Kiss1 neurons regulates fertility in females.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data from genetic mouse models presented in Figures 1-3.

claim: Deletion of Mc4r from Kiss1 neurons in female mice replicates the reproductive impairments of Mc4r KO mice without inducing obesity.
source: In vivo, deletion of Mc4r from Kiss1 neurons in female mice replicates the reproductive impairments of Mc4r KO mice without inducing obesity.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2A showing normal body weight and Figure 2B-T showing reproductive impairments in Kiss1-Mc4r KO mice.

claim: Re-insertion of Mc4r in Kiss1 neurons of Mc4r null mice restores estrous cyclicity and LH pulsatility without reducing their obese phenotype.
source: Conversely, re-insertion of Mc4r in Kiss1 neurons of Mc4r null mice restores estrous cyclicity and LH pulsatility without reducing their obese phenotype.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 3D showing persistent obesity and Figure 3E-J showing restored reproductive function in Kiss1Cre:Mc4rloxTB mice.

claim: Mc4r activation excites Kiss1ARH neurons through direct synaptic actions.
source: In vitro, we dissect the specific action of Mc4r on Kiss1ARH versus Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons and show that Mc4r activation excites Kiss1ARH neurons through direct synaptic actions.
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data in Figure 4 showing inward currents in response to MC4R agonists.

claim: Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons are normally inhibited by MC4R activation except under elevated estradiol levels.
source: In contrast, Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons are normally inhibited by MC4R activation except under elevated estradiol levels, thus facilitating the activation of Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons to induce the LH surge driving ovulation in females.
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data in Figure 5 showing outward currents in OVX mice and reversal with estradiol treatment.

claim: POMCARH neurons acting through MC4R directly regulate reproductive function in females by stimulating the 'pulse generator' activity of Kiss1ARH neurons.
source: Our findings demonstrate that POMCARH neurons acting through MC4R directly regulate reproductive function in females by stimulating the 'pulse generator' activity of Kiss1ARH neurons and restricting the activation of Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons to the time of the estradiol-dependent LH surge
evidence: This is a synthesis of the in vivo and in vitro findings presented in Figures 2-5.

claim: POMCARH neurons restrict the activation of Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons to the time of the estradiol-dependent LH surge.
source: Our findings demonstrate that POMCARH neurons acting through MC4R directly regulate reproductive function in females by stimulating the 'pulse generator' activity of Kiss1ARH neurons and restricting the activation of Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons to the time of the estradiol-dependent LH surge
evidence: This is supported by the estradiol-dependent reversal of MC4R inhibition in Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons shown in Figure 5.

claim: The melanocortin system provides a novel pathway for the metabolic regulation of fertility.
source: and thus unveil a novel pathway of the metabolic regulation of fertility by the melanocortin system.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined in vivo and in vitro findings of the study.

claim: Obesity rates have increased in Western societies in recent decades.
source: Obesity rates have skyrocketed in Western societies in the last decades, resulting in an alarming rise in comorbidities that place a significant burden on healthcare systems.
evidence: This is general knowledge about public health trends.

claim: The increase in obesity correlates with a decrease in fertility rates.
source: The increase in obesity correlates with a decrease in fertility rates, leading to conception challenges that are experienced by approximately 15% of couples in the United States currently (Health, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Health, 2020.

claim: Approximately 15% of couples in the United States experience conception challenges.
source: The increase in obesity correlates with a decrease in fertility rates, leading to conception challenges that are experienced by approximately 15% of couples in the United States currently (Health, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Health, 2020.

claim: MC4R binds α-melanocyte stimulating hormone (αMSH), an agonist product of the pro-opiomelanocortin (Pomc) gene.
source: The melanocortin 4 receptor (MC4R) binds (1) α-melanocyte stimulating hormone (αMSH), an agonist product of the pro-opiomelanocortin (Pomc) gene, and (2) the inverse agonist, agouti-related peptide (AgRP), to regulate food intake and energy expenditure (Andermann and Lowell, 2017; Cone, 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citations (Andermann and Lowell, 2017; Cone, 2006).

claim: MC4R binds agouti-related peptide (AgRP), an inverse agonist.

evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citations (Andermann and Lowell, 2017; Cone, 2006).

claim: The role of MC4R on food intake is largely mediated by neurons located in the paraventricular nucleus of the hypothalamus (PVN).
source: While the role of MC4R on food intake is largely mediated by neurons located in the paraventricular nucleus of the hypothalamus (PVN) (Shah et al., 2014), its expression in the brain is widespread (Wang et al., 2020) with the specific function of the different MC4R-expressing neurons in areas beyond the PVN remaining to be fully explored.
evidence: This is supported by citations (Shah et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2020).

claim: MC4R expression in the brain is widespread.

claim: Inactivating mutations in MC4R are a leading cause of monogenic obesity in humans.

claim: Inactivating mutations in MC4R cause excessive obesity and hyperphagia in mice.

claim: MC4R mutations are associated with higher incidence of hypogonadotropic hypogonadism in humans.
source: Scant evidence in humans shows an association between MC4R mutations and higher incidence of hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (Hainerová et al., 2011), alterations in the timing of puberty onset (Doulla et al., 2014), and polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS; Batarfi et al., 2019); however, other studies have shown no association between MC4R and reproductive disorders (Farooqi et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by a citation (Hainerová et al., 2011).

claim: The role of MC4R signaling in reproductive function in humans remains controversial.
source: Therefore, the role of MC4R signaling in reproductive function in humans remains controversial despite the clear association found in mice.
evidence: This is an inference based on the conflicting evidence cited in the previous sentence.

claim: The lower inhibitory tone of dynorphin correlates with the higher basal LH levels in Kiss1- Mc4r KO mice.

evidence: This is supported by data presented in Figure 3F-J.

claim: The melanocortin action on Kiss1 neurons is required for the normal control of gonadotropin release.

evidence: This is an inference based on the recovery of LH pulsatility in Kiss1Cre:Mc4rloxTB mice.

claim: Kiss1Cre: Mc4rloxTB mice presented fewer corpora lutea than controls, similar to Mc4rloxTB mice.

claim: An ovulatory impairment persists in Kiss1Cre: Mc4rloxTB mice.
source: Despite these significant improvements in reproductive function, Kiss1Cre: Mc4rloxTB mice presented fewer corpora lutea than controls (0.80 ± 0.80), similar to Mc4rloxTB mice, suggesting that an ovulatory impairment persists (Figure 3K, L).
evidence: This is an inference based on the persistent reduction in corpora lutea in Kiss1Cre:Mc4rloxTB mice.

claim: Metabolic signals derived from the obese phenotype and/or the absence of the direct action of MC4R in GnRH neurons may prevent the complete recovery of ovulation in Kiss1Cre: Mc4rloxTB mice.
source: It is possible that the metabolic signals derived from their obese phenotype, and/or the absence of the direct action of MC4R in GnRH neurons (Israel et al., 2012; Roa and Herbison, 2012) prevents the complete recovery of ovulation in Kiss1Cre: Mc4rloxTB mice.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanisms underlying the persistent ovulatory impairment, supported by citations (Israel et al., 2012; Roa and Herbison, 2012).

claim: Mc4rloxTB and Kiss1Cre: Mc4rloxTB mice displayed significantly lower testosterone levels than control mice in diestrus.

claim: Mc4rloxTB and Kiss1Cre: Mc4rloxTB mice displayed significantly lower AMH levels than control mice in diestrus.

claim: A PCOS-like reproductive phenotype mediated by the lack of melanocortin signaling can be excluded in Mc4rloxTB and Kiss1Cre: Mc4rloxTB mice.
source: Therefore, we can exclude, once again, a PCOS-like reproductive phenotype mediated by the lack of melanocortin signaling.
evidence: This is an inference based on the low testosterone and AMH levels in these mice.

claim: Focal application of melanotan II (MTII, ~250 nM) elicited a small inward current in half of the isolated Kiss1ARH cells.
source: Focal application of the high-affinity melanocortin receptor agonist melanotan II (MTII, ~250 nM) elicited a small inward current in half of the isolated Kiss1ARH cells (10/21) (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data presented in Figure 4B.

claim: There was no significant difference in the average MTII-induced current in Kiss1ARH neurons between OVX and OVX+E2 females.
source: Next, we examined if the E2 state affected MTII response by recording from Kiss1ARH neurons from OVX females and found two-thirds (6/9 cells) responded, but there was no significant difference in the average current (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data presented in Figure 4C.

claim: THIQ (100 nM) was able to elicit an excitatory inward current in Kiss1ARH neurons.
source: Similar to MTII, THIQ was able to elicit an excitatory inward current in Kiss1ARH neurons (4/5 cells, –7.4 ± 0.5 pA), indicating MC4R activation is sufficient (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data presented in Figure 4D.

claim: MC4R activation is sufficient to invoke a postsynaptic response in Kiss1ARH neurons.
source: Similar to MTII, THIQ was able to elicit an excitatory inward current in Kiss1ARH neurons (4/5 cells, –7.4 ± 0.5 pA), indicating MC4R activation is sufficient (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is an inference based on the response to the selective MC4R agonist THIQ.

claim: High-frequency stimulation of POMC fibers elicited a slow inward current in Kiss1ARH neurons.
source: Using the AAV-driven expression of channelrhodopsin in adult PomcCre mice, high-frequency stimulation elicited a slow inward current in Kiss1 neurons.
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data presented in Figure 4F.

claim: POMC neurons make direct monosynaptic connections with Kiss1ARH neurons.
source: A direct synaptic projection from POMC to Kiss1ARH neuron (post hoc identified) was confirmed using the 'rescue' protocol
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data presented in Figure 4H showing rescue of the postsynaptic response with K+ channel blockers.

claim: Treatment with E2 increased the probability of glutamate release from POMC neurons onto Kiss1ARH neurons.
source: As anticipated, we found that treatment with E2 increased the probability of glutamate release from POMC neurons onto Kiss1ARH neurons based on the significant decrease in the paired pulse ratio of the two stimuli (Herman et al., 2014; Figure 4J).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data presented in Figure 4I, J.

claim: Kiss1ARH neurons are excited by the glutamatergic input from POMC neurons in an E2-dependent manner.
source: Therefore, Kiss1ARH neurons are excited by the glutamatergic input from POMC neurons in an E2-dependent manner.
evidence: This is an inference based on the increased glutamate release probability with E2 treatment.

claim: High-frequency stimulation of POMC fibers evoked an excitatory inward current in Kiss1ARH neurons that was blocked by the selective MC3/4R antagonist SHU 9119.
source: Indeed, high-frequency stimulation evoked an excitatory inward current (Figure 4K) that was blocked by the selective MC3/4R antagonist SHU 9119 (Figure 4L).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data presented in Figure 4K, L.

claim: Pretreatment with naloxone increased the likelihood and magnitude of a response to high-frequency stimulation in Kiss1ARH neurons.
source: In order to isolate melanocortin signaling, we pretreated slices with the non-selective opioid antagonist naloxone (1 μM) and found an increase in the likelihood and magnitude of a response to high-frequency stimulation (9/23, 40%, mean inward current: –7.6 ± 2.9 pA) (Figure 4M).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data presented in Figure 4M.

claim: There are excitatory glutamatergic and peptidergic inputs from POMC to Kiss1ARH neurons.
source: Together, these optogenetic findings reinforced our pharmacological results showing that Kiss1ARH neurons are excited by MCR agonists. Additional studies would need to be done to identify the cation conductance that is affected by the MC4R signaling cascade in Kiss1ARH neurons, but clearly, we have established that there are excitatory glutamatergic and peptidergic inputs from POMC to Kiss1ARH neurons.
evidence: This is a synthesis of the optogenetic and pharmacological findings presented in Figure 4.

claim: POMC fibers densely innervated the AVPV/PeN area.
source: First, we used immunocytochemistry to label fibers expressing αMSH to demonstrate that POMC fibers densely innervated the AVPV/PeN area (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data presented in Figure 5A.

claim: POMC neurons make direct monosynaptic connections with Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons.
source: We recorded a direct glutamatergic synaptic response following optogenetic stimulation in six neurons, which was further verified through pharmacological 'rescue' of the synaptic response in the majority (5/6) neurons tested (Figure 5C), indicating that POMC neurons make direct monosynaptic connections with Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons.
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data presented in Figure 5C.

claim: Bath application of MTII (500 nM) generated an inhibitory outward current in Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons from OVX females.
source: Surprisingly, we consistently measured an outward (inhibitory) current that could be reversed on washout of MTII (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data presented in Figure 5D.

claim: The outward current induced by MTII in Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons was associated with an increase in K+ conductance.
source: This outward current was associated with an increase in K+ conductance based on the current-voltage plot (i.e., the outward current reversed at ~EK+, Figure 5E).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data presented in Figure 5E.

claim: MC4R may be coupled to activation of inwardly rectifying K+ channels in Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons.
source: Also, the inwardly rectifying I/V could indicate that MC4R is coupled to activation of inwardly rectifying K+ channels, as has been previously reported for MC4R signaling in pre-autonomic parasympathetic neurons in the brainstem (Sohn et al., 2013).
evidence: This is speculation based on the I/V relationship and a citation to similar findings in other neurons (Sohn et al., 2013).

claim: STX pretreatment resulted in either a greatly attenuated outward current or even an inward current in response to MTII in Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons.
source: Indeed, the outward current (inhibitory) response to MTII was completely abrogated and even reversed by STX (Figure 5F, G).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data presented in Figure 5F, G.

claim: Estrogen receptor activation can rapidly uncouple (i.e., desensitize) the MC4R inhibitory response in Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons.
source: Therefore, estrogen receptor activation can rapidly uncouple (i.e., desensitize) the MC4R inhibitory response in Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons.
evidence: This is an inference based on the reversal of MC4R inhibition by STX, a Gq-mER agonist.

claim: Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons were more inhibited by MTII in vehicle-treated, OVX females compared to E2-treated, OVX females.
source: We next investigated the response in vehicle-treated, OVX females. Indeed, Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons were even more inhibited by the same MTII exposure (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data presented in Figure 5G.

claim: MC4R appears to be coupled to the opening of K+ channels in Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons.
source: Therefore, in contrast to Kiss1ARH neurons, the MC4R appears to be coupled to the opening of K+ channels in Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons.
evidence: This is an inference based on the outward current and I/V relationship data.

claim: MTII had no significant effect on the frequency of glutamatergic mEPSCs in Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons.
source: We found there was no significant effect on the frequency (Figure 5H)
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data presented in Figure 5H.

claim: MTII had a significant effect on the amplitude of glutamatergic mEPSCs in Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons.
source: but there was an effect on the amplitude (Figure 5I).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological data presented in Figure 5I.

claim: The effect of MTII on mEPSC amplitude supports a postsynaptic locus of STX's effects in Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons.
source: This further supports a postsynaptic locus of STX's effects.
evidence: This is an inference based on the mEPSC amplitude data.

evidence: This is a synthesis of the in vivo and in vitro findings of the study.

evidence: This is supported by a citation (Lam et al., 2021).

source: While Mc4r has been documented in the ovary (Chen et al., 2017)
evidence: This is supported by a citation (Chen et al., 2017).

evidence: This is supported by a citation (Batarfi et al., 2019).

source: However, our mouse models failed to display higher levels of circulating androgens or AMH, two of the hallmarks of PCOS (Dewailly et al., 2020), suggesting that melanocortin signaling is unlikely to be a main contributing factor in the development of this syndrome.
evidence: This is an inference based on the normal testosterone and AMH levels in the mouse models.

claim: Mc4r signaling excites Kiss1ARH neurons.
source: We further investigated this and found that Mc4r signaling excites Kiss1ARH neurons

source: and inhibits Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons in an estradiol-dependent manner.

However, cell-attached recordings do not measure a direct response in isolated Kiss1ARH neurons but rather the summation of multiple synaptic inputs to Kiss1ARH neurons.
evidence: This is an explanation for the discrepancy between the current findings and previous studies, supported by citations (Manfredi-Lozano et al., 2016; Sabine Hessler and Herbison, 2020).

claim: POMCARH neurons are able to exert a precise regulatory role of the GnRH pulse generator through the excitatory action of glutamate and the inhibitory action of β-endorphin.
source: The modulatory actions of POMCARH neuronal projections to Kiss1ARH neurons can also occur through (1) the excitatory action of glutamate in a process that is facilitated in the presence of estradiol, in line with previous publications (Qiu et al., 2018; Stincic et al., 2018), and (2) the inhibitory action of β-endorphin, suggesting that POMCARH neurons are able to exert a precise regulatory role of the GnRH pulse generator, that is Kiss1ARH neurons, in response to metabolic challenges.
evidence: This is an inference based on the optogenetic and pharmacological findings, supported by citations (Qiu et al., 2018; Stincic et al., 2018).

claim: Rapid estrogen signaling may act to ease transitions between states.
source: Rapid estrogen signaling may act to ease transitions between states.
evidence: This is speculation about the functional significance of rapid estrogen signaling.

source: Membrane-delimited E2 actions can quickly attenuate or enhance coupling between receptors and signaling cascades.
evidence: This is established knowledge about membrane estrogen receptor signaling.

claim: Parallel mechanisms acting on different timescales are particularly important in the abbreviated mouse reproductive cycle.
source: Considering the abbreviated mouse reproductive cycle, parallel mechanisms acting on different timescales are particularly important.
evidence: This is an inference about the functional significance of the findings in the context of mouse reproductive physiology.

claim: The inhibitory tone of MC4R signaling on Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons might be involved in the timing of puberty onset.
source: This data suggests that the inhibitory tone of MC4R signaling on Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons might also be involved in the timing of puberty onset
evidence: This is speculation based on the advanced puberty onset in Kiss1-Mc4r KO females.

claim: Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons play a role in sexual maturation.
source: which in turn suggests a role for this female-specific population of Kiss1 neurons in sexual maturation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the advanced puberty onset in Kiss1-Mc4r KO females.

claim: Metabolic cues, through the regulation of the melanocortin output onto Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons, are essential for the timing and magnitude of the GnRH/LH surge.
source: Furthermore, our findings suggest that metabolic cues, through the regulation of the melanocortin output onto Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons, are essential for the timing and magnitude of the GnRH/LH surge.
evidence: This is an inference based on the estradiol-dependent inhibition of Kiss1AVPV/PeN neurons by MC4R.

claim: The melanocortin–kisspeptin pathway is one of the multiple pathways essential for the metabolic regulation of the HPG axis.
source: This study suggests that the melanocortin–kisspeptin pathway is one of the multiple pathways essential for the metabolic regulation of the HPG axis.
evidence: This is a synthesis of the findings of the study.

claim: MC4R has a differential regulatory action in the neural control of GnRH/LH release, participating in both the surge and the pulse-like modes of LH release through the cellular regulation of Kiss1 neurons.
source: Altogether, our data reveal a differential regulatory action of MC4R in the neural control of GnRH/LH release, participating in both the surge (E2-treated, ovariectomized female) and the pulse-like (ovariectomized female) modes of LH release through the cellular regulation of Kiss1 neurons
evidence: This is a synthesis of the in vivo and in vitro findings.

claim: The reproductive abnormalities often attributed to obesity in MC4R-deficient patients may not be caused by the excess in body weight but by a deficiency in MC4R signaling directly at the level of Kiss1 neurons.
source: These findings are important because the reproductive abnormalities often attributed to obesity in MC4R-deficient patients may not be caused by the excess in body weight but, at least in part, by a deficiency in MC4R signaling directly at the level of Kiss1 neurons that affects predominantly the ability to mount a preovulatory LH surge.
evidence: This is an inference about the implications of the findings for understanding human reproductive disorders.

claim: MC4R deficiency affects predominantly the ability to mount a preovulatory LH surge.
source: These findings are important because the reproductive abnormalities often attributed to obesity in MC4R-deficient patients may not be caused by the excess in body weight but, at least in part, by a deficiency in MC4R signaling directly at the level of Kiss1 neurons that affects predominantly the ability to mount a preovulatory LH surge.
evidence: This is supported by the blunted LH surge in Kiss1-Mc4r KO females (Figure 2M).
